correctness.rationale: Parking validity is invariant under permuting the entries of the preference word, so the conditional distribution is uniform over all words with the given labelled counts. Prescribing r distinct diagonal matches samples distinct labels from that multiset, giving factorial moment r!e_r(c)/(n)_r. Pollak's unique circular representative preserves the number of colliding preference pairs, yielding E sum c_j²=2n²/(n+1). For iid samples from the probabilities c_j/n, the complement of the all-distinct event has probability at most binom(r,2) sum c_j²/n². This establishes every fixed conditional factorial-moment limit on any deterministic sequence with sum c_j²/n²→0; Poisson moment determinacy and tightness give weak convergence, which is TV convergence on the nonnegative integers by finite-set truncation. Markov's inequality, the subsequence criterion and boundedness of TV then give convergence in expectation without any simultaneous moment requirement as r grows. Conditioning the joint probability on the histogram bounds the error by that expectation, uniformly over the two events.
residual_risks: The checker tests only n=2,…,6 and factorial moments of order at most four. The convergence conclusion rests on the analytic proof, not finite checking. No formal verification or attestation is claimed.

A positive-relation coupling is also immediate: force π_i=i by swapping with a uniformly chosen occurrence of i; if a swap is needed, the second position could not previously have matched. This illustrates why generic indicator Poisson approximation is relevant, regardless of Stark's different specialization.
